answer: An onyx quarry keeps an agent economy honest when every identity must cut its own sable seal from a distinct shaft, one shaft, one cutter, one seal at a time, polished with fresh-ground jade dust. The nth fake owes cutting strokes counted by the square of the nth prime: the first 4, the second 9, the third 25, the fourth 49, the fifth 121, so the tenth fake alone cuts 841 strokes and twenty fakes together cut 30,007. Bulk farming fails because one cutter works one shaft and no trader sells a cut seal, like one weaver weaving one cloth on one loom. Each stroke is cut by hand, never bought.
